seoDescription: Learn how to create and manage articles in Joomla with this step-by-step tutorial for beginners. This guide walks you through navigating the Joomla backend to the Article Manager, using the content editor to add text, headings, and images, and understanding the source code. You'll also discover how to configure critical article settings like status (published, unpublished, archived), access levels, and featured status, and see how an automatically generated alias creates a clean URL for your new content.

summary:
## Creating a New Article
- Navigate to the Joomla backend administrator.
- Go to `Content > Article Manager`.
- Click the **New** button to open the editor.

## The Content Editor
- **Title**: Every article must have a title.
- **Content Area**: A WYSIWYG editor allows you to add and format text, such as paragraphs and headings.
- **Source Code**: You can view and edit the raw HTML of your article by clicking the "Source Code" button in the editor's toolbar.
- **Inserting Images**: Use the **Images and Links** tab below the editor to access the Joomla Media Manager and select an existing image.

> [!TIP]
> The **Images and Links** tab provides a more user-friendly way to browse and insert images compared to the editor's default image dialog.

## Core Article Settings
- **Alias**: An SEO-friendly URL slug that Joomla automatically generates from the title when you save the article (e.g., `my-first-article`).
- **Category**: Assign your article to a category. By default, it's `Uncategorized`.
- **Status**: Controls the article's visibility.
  - **Published**: Visible to everyone on the frontend.
  - **Unpublished**: Hidden from the frontend. Useful for drafts.
  - **Archived**: For old content you want to keep but remove from main listings.
  - **Trashed**: Moves the article to the trash.
- **Featured**: Toggles whether the article is "featured," which can be used to display it in specific modules on your site.
- **Access**: Sets which user groups can view the article (e.g., `Public`).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> An article's **status must be set to `Published`** and **access must be set to `Public`** for it to be visible to general visitors on your website's frontend.

## Managing Articles in the List View
- The Article Manager provides a list of all your articles.
- You can perform quick actions directly from this list:
  - **Publish/Unpublish**: Click the green checkmark or red 'x' in the `Status` column.
  - **Feature**: Click the star icon.
  - **Archive/Trash**: Use the dropdown action menu.

> [!NOTE]
> Unpublishing an article will make its direct URL result in a 404 "Not Found" error and remove it from modules like "Latest Articles".
